shapes.alt: Small talk: two people say 'Nice day, isn't it?' and 'Yes, it is!'

slides.notes:
Welcome learners as they arrive. Each learner writes a first name on a name tag.
Point to the title and read it: "Tell me more." Say: "Tonight we keep a conversation going. We don't stop at one word."
Read the three lines under "Today you will". Give one quick example of each: "Really? Why?" (a follow-up question) • "I take the bus because it's cheap." (a reason) • "My car broke down, so I took the bus." (a result).
Keep it short. Don't explain the grammar now. Go straight to the warm-up.
Source: Level3_Lesson1.md (Topic; At a glance: Objectives; Step 1).

slides.title: Tell Me More

runs.t: I can ask about my week.
I can ask a follow-up question.
I can give a reason with because.
I can say a result with so.
I can write about a classmate.
By the end of class, you can do these five things.

slides.notes:
Read each goal slowly. Learners repeat.
Goal 1 is review from Level 2: do = now (What do you do on weekends?), did = the past (What did you do last weekend?), going to = the future (What are you going to do this weekend?).
Goals 2 to 4 are new tonight: follow-up questions (Really? Why? What happened? How was it? What about you?), because + a reason, so + a result.
Goal 5: later tonight, learners read a community center flyer and write 3 sentences about a classmate.
Say: "In Level 3, don't stop at one word. Give a reason. Ask a question back."
"We check at 7:25" = the Progress Check, the first can-do self-check. It is not a test grade.
Source: Level3_Lesson1.md (At a glance: Objectives; How Our Class Works; Progress Check).
slides.title: Today's Goals

shapes.name: Name tag
shapes.alt: Follow-up question: 'I got a new job.' then 'Really? Where?'

runs.t: What did you do last weekend?
What are you going to do this weekend?

slides.notes:
Step 1 · 6:00–6:10 · 10 min. Pairs. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 group of 3. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs.
Before class, write on the board: What did you do last weekend? → Really? How was it?
Model with one learner: ask "What did you do last weekend?" The learner answers. Then say "Really? How was it?" Point to the second question and say: "This is a follow-up question. It asks for more."
Round 1 (4 min): A asks the question, B answers, A asks one follow-up. Switch.
Round 2 (4 min): new partner. Add to the board: What are you going to do this weekend? → Why?
Late arrivals join any pair as a group of 3. If behind: one round only.
Privacy: learners choose what to share. Any answer can be invented. "I don't want to say" is always OK.
Source: Level3_Lesson1.md (Step 1; Teacher notes: Privacy).

slides.title: One Question, One Follow-Up

runs.t: Work with a partner or a group.
Ask a follow-up. Give a reason.

slides.notes:
Step 2 · 6:10–6:15 · Orientation · 5 min. Whole class. Learners open the Student Pages to How Our Class Works.
Show the times: class 6:00, break 6:45, back 7:00, end 7:30.
Say and show the 3 rules: (1) "English in class. A classmate can help you for a few seconds. Then back to English." (2) "Homework every week. About 15 minutes." (3) "Phones are OK for the audio and a dictionary."
Left side: the task words. We use the same short task words every week. Read each line; act it out (hand to ear for Listen, write in the air for Write, draw a circle for Circle).
Point to the Task Words page and say: "You can write them in your language here." Point to the My language column. No one has to.
Also say: "In this class, we don't give one-word answers. We give a reason, and we ask a question back."
If behind: show the times and say the 3 rules only.
Source: Level3_Lesson1.md (Step 2; How to Use This Plan: Instructions; Task Words; How Our Class Works).

slides.title: Before You Listen

slides.notes:
Task A. Read the 4 lines with the class first: has good news, has bad news, is very tired, has a new job.
Play 1: play the whole audio (about 1:31). Learners check Elena or David on their page.
Pairs compare. Then check together: click to show the answer. Each click circles one answer, in order 1 to 4: 1 Elena, 2 David, 3 David, 4 Elena.
Then read Tasks B and C together (1 min), so learners know what to listen for in play 2.
Source: Level3_Lesson1.md (Step 4; Listening Task A; Answer key).
slides.title: Listening A

runs.t: 1. David's car broke down on Tuesday.
2. David took a taxi to work this week.
3. The car is maybe going to be ready next Friday.
4. Elena's new job is at a school.

slides.notes:
Task B (play 2). Before play 2, read Tasks B and C together (1 min) so learners know what to listen for.
Play 2: play the whole audio again. Learners check True or False on their page (and write because or so for Task C).
Pairs compare. Then check together: click to show the answer. Each click circles one answer, in order 1 to 6.
Answers: 1 True • 2 False (he took the bus) • 3 True • 4 False (at a hospital) • 5 True • 6 False (he starts at six).
A third play is fine if the class needs it.
Source: Level3_Lesson1.md (Step 4; Listening Task B; Answer key).
slides.title: Listening B

runs.t: David: ____ my car broke down on Tuesday.
Now it's at the mechanic, ____ I took the bus to work.
Yes, I love it, ____ the people are really friendly.
It's only ten minutes from my apartment, ____ I don't need a car.
I really need my car, ____ my job is far away.

slides.notes:
Task C (play 2, with Task B). Learners write because or so in each line.
Pairs compare. Then check together: click to show the answer. Each click shows one answer, in order 1 to 5.
Answers: 1 Because • 2 so • 3 because • 4 so • 5 because.
Line 2 is short on the slide. The full line on the page is: "Now it's at the mechanic, so I took the bus to work every day this week."
If behind: do Task C together on the board, reading the lines yourself.
Source: Level3_Lesson1.md (Step 4; Listening Task C; Answer key).
slides.title: Listening C

runs.t: What about you? How was your week?

slides.notes:
Answer check. Three sentences in Task B are false. Ask: "What's the right answer?" Learners say it first. Then click to show the answer. Each click shows one answer, in order 2, 4, 6.
2: David took the bus (not a taxi). • 4: Elena's new job is at a hospital (not a school). • 6: David starts at six (not seven).
"Say it" (2 min): read the 2 lines: "Really? Why?" and "What about you? How was your week?" The class repeats each line twice.
Make Really? go up and sound interested.
Source: Level3_Lesson1.md (Step 4: "Say it"; Answer key: Listening Task B).

runs.t: do = now  ·  did = past  ·  going to = future
you going to do this weekend?

slides.notes:
Step 5 · 6:34–6:45 · Grammar Q&A · 11 min (slides 13 to 18). Whole class, then pairs.
Show the Grammar page. The left side is the question. The right side is the answer.
Box 1 (review, 2 min): read a question. The class answers from the right side. Then click to show the answer. Each click shows one answer, in order 1, 2, 3.
Point to the time words: on weekends (now), last weekend (the past), this weekend (the future). do = now, did = the past, going to = the future.
Don't re-teach. Level 2 taught these.
Source: Level3_Lesson1.md (Step 5; Grammar Box 1).

runs.t: That's great! When do you start?
My week was busy. How was your week?
What do you like about it?

slides.notes:
Box 2 (3 min). A follow-up question is a second question about the same topic. It shows you are listening and keeps the conversation going.
Read a sentence from the left. The class says a follow-up question. Then click to show the follow-ups for that line. Each click shows one row, in order 1 to 6.
Then say your own news ("I have a new cat!") and wait for follow-ups.
To ask the question back, say: "What about you?" or "And you?"
Learners who are new to the class can use Box 2 on their page as a script.
Source: Level3_Lesson1.md (Step 5; Grammar Box 2; Questions and answers; Teacher notes).

slides.title: Follow-up Questions

shapes.name: Picture first name
shapes.alt: Reason: thinking face and light bulb; 'Why?' 'Because it's cheap. = the reason'

runs.t: Because + the reason. It answers Why?

slides.notes:
Box 3 (with Box 4, 3 min). Write on the board: because + reason.
Read a question from the left. The class answers with Because. Then click to show the answer. Each click shows one answer, in order 1, 2, 3.
Point to do / does / did: Why do you…? (now) • Why does she…? (she, now) • Why did you…? (the past). Don't forget do / did in the question.
In a conversation, after Why?, you can start with Because: "Why? Because I was tired." In writing, join it to the other sentence: "I stayed home because I was tired."
Check questions: "I stayed home ___ I was sick." (because) • "Why ___ you take the bus?" (do)
Typical mistake: "Why you take the bus?" Say the right form clearly: "Why do you take the bus?" The learner repeats.
Source: Level3_Lesson1.md (Step 5; Grammar Box 3; Questions and answers; Teacher notes).
Picture: Twemoji graphics by Twitter, Inc. and other contributors (https://github.com/jdecked/twemoji), CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); resized and combined, with drawn speech bubbles and labels (images/CREDITS.md).
slides.title: Why…? Because…

shapes.name: Picture letter
shapes.alt: Bad news: worried face and rain cloud

slides.notes:
Box 4 (with Box 3, 3 min). Write on the board: because + reason, so + result.
Read one row from each box. Click to show the result lines (2 clicks: the white box, then the blue box).
Ask: "My car broke down. Is that the reason or the result?" (reason) "I took the bus." (result).
because comes before the reason; so comes before the result. Put a comma before so. Use one word, not both: "I was tired, so I stayed home." or "I stayed home because I was tired."
Quick test: "Why?" is answered by the because part.
Check question: "I was sick, ___ I stayed home." (so)
Pair drill (last 3 min): A asks a Why…? question. B answers with because. A asks one follow-up. Switch. If behind: skip the pair drill; Talk Time practices it.
Source: Level3_Lesson1.md (Step 5; Grammar Box 4; Questions and answers; Teacher notes).

slides.title: …, so… (the result) because

runs.t: I'm learning English ____ I want a better job.
It was raining, ____ I took an umbrella.
She likes her neighbors ____ they are very friendly.
The store was closed, ____ we went home.
He drinks coffee every morning ____ he starts work at 6:00.
Is it the reason or the result?
My coworker was sick, ____ I worked late.

slides.notes:
Practice (part of Step 5). Learners write because or so in each sentence on their Grammar page.
Ask for each line: "Is the next part the reason or the result?" Reason = because. Result = so.
Pairs check. Then click to show the answer. Each click shows one answer, in order 1 to 6.
Answers: 1 because • 2 so • 3 because • 4 so • 5 because • 6 so.
Source: Level3_Lesson1.md (Grammar: Practice; Answer key: Grammar practice).
slides.title: Because or So?

shapes.name: Picture name tag
shapes.alt: Reason: thinking face and light bulb; 'Why?' 'Because it's cheap. = the reason'

runs.t: Because I was tired, so I stayed home.

slides.notes:
Common mistakes (never skip this table). Read a line from Don't say. Ask: "What's the right way?" Learners try first. Then click to show the right form. Each click shows one line, in order 1 to 6.
1: use because or so, not both. • 2: Why do you…? (add do) • 3: What did you do…? (did before you) • 4: Because + reason (no of) • 5: I'm going to… (add am) • 6: don't give one-word answers; add a detail and ask the question back.
Say the right form clearly; the learner repeats.
Tip: in English, a one-word answer can sound unfriendly or bored. Add a reason (because…) or ask a question back (What about you?).
Source: Level3_Lesson1.md (Grammar: Common mistakes; Tip for speakers of other languages; Teacher notes: Typical mistakes).

runs.t: A asks. B gives a reason.
Ask Why…? Answer with because. Ask one follow-up. Switch.

slides.notes:
Pair drill (last 3 min of Step 5). Pairs.
A asks a Why…? question (use Box 3). B answers with because. A asks one follow-up question (use Box 2). Then switch.
Model it with one learner first: "Why did you stay home?" → "Because I was tired." → "Are you OK?"
Check it: ask "Do you write or speak?" (speak) "How many follow-up questions?" (one). Then go.
Mixed levels: stronger learners ask more follow-ups and give two reasons. New learners read Box 2 and Box 3 on their page as a script.
If behind: skip the pair drill. Talk Time practices it.
Source: Level3_Lesson1.md (Step 5: Pair drill; Grammar Boxes 2 and 3; How to Use This Plan; Teacher notes).

slides.title: Pair Drill

shapes.name: Picture classmates
shapes.alt: Chat: two people, a speech balloon, and a coffee cup

runs.t: What do you do on weekends?
In the park, because it's free.

slides.notes:
Step 6 · 7:00–7:12 · Talk Time: The Three-Question Rule · 12 min. Inside–outside circles: the inner circle faces out, the outer circle faces in.
15 learners: two circles of 7–8 (the teacher or one trio fills a gap). 7–8 learners: one circle. 5 or fewer: sit at one table and rotate seats.
The rule: the inner circle has a question card. A asks the card question. B answers. A must ask two follow-up questions. B must use because or so at least once. Then switch roles, and the outer circle moves one person to the right.
Model with one learner (1 min): "What do you do on weekends?" → "I play soccer." → "Really? Where?" → "In the park, because it's free." → "Who do you play with?" (Each click shows the next step.)
Do 3–4 rounds of about 2 minutes. Learners write one answer on their Talk Time page after each round.
Follow-ups on the board: Really? Why? What happened? How was it? What about you?
Baseline snapshot: while learners talk, call about 5 learners, one at a time, for 2 minutes, and use the checklist after the answer key. Do the rest in Weeks 2 and 3.
Privacy: learners choose what to share; any answer can be invented. Praise every follow-up you hear, even a simple "Really?"
If behind: two rounds only.
Source: Level3_Lesson1.md (Step 6; Talk Time page; Grouping toolkit; Teacher notes).

shapes.alt: Introduce: a man introduces a woman: 'This is Ana.' 'Nice to meet you!'

runs.t: Rosa takes the bus because she doesn't have a car.
Give it to me at the door.

slides.notes:
Step 7 · 7:12–7:17 · Exit Ticket + Homework · 5 min · NEVER SKIP.
Exit ticket: each learner writes two sentences on a slip: one about a classmate ("Rosa takes the bus because she doesn't have a car.") and one with so. Collect the slips at the door.
Homework: open the Homework page. Do item 1 together. Say: "About 15 minutes. Bring it next week."
Homework items: 1 answer 3 Why questions with because; 2 ask a friend, family member, or coworker 2 questions, with one follow-up each, and write the answers; 3 join two sentences with so; 4 review: write 2 sentences about last weekend.
Source: Level3_Lesson1.md (Step 7; Homework page).

slides.title: Before You Go

runs.t: I can ask a follow-up question.
I can give a reason with because.
I can say a result with so.
I can talk about my week, my past, and my plans.
A. Listen. Circle the best follow-up.

slides.notes:
Progress Check · 7:25–7:30 · first can-do self-check · 5 min. Individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
Part A: read each sentence slowly, 2 times. Learners circle the best follow-up on their page. Then click to show the answer (one click per item, 1 to 4).
Say: 1 "I'm really tired today." (a, Why?) • 2 "I went to a wedding on Saturday." (b, How was it?) • 3 "I have good news!" (a, Really? What is it?) • 4 "My phone is broken." (b, Oh no! What happened?)
Parts B and C: learners do them alone. Walk around and help with the instructions only. B answers: 1 because, 2 so, 3 so, 4 because. C: any good follow-up question (for example Really? Where? / How was it?).
Part D: read each "I can…" line aloud and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "With a little help." 😐 "Not yet."
Scoring: A /4 + B /4 + C /2 = /10. This is not a test grade. It shows who needs more help with follow-ups (A, C) and with because / so (B).
Collect the pages (or check them at the start of Week 2). If behind: do the Progress Check in Week 2 at 6:00, while learners arrive.
Source: Level3_Lesson1.md (Progress Check step; Progress Check page; Answer key).
